problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{22}$ equal to zero.*
worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{22}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -3 \\ -5 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -3 \\ -5 & -5 & 10 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
